units: Lev. R. s. 34 רש מן הנכסים the poor man is called râsh, because he is dispossessed of property.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 34:11">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Proverbs 29:13">Prov. XXIX, 13</cite>) <he>זהו רש בתורה</he> this means one bare of learning.
<cite ref="Proverbs 29:13">Ib.</cite> (ref. to ib. XXII, 2) <he>אמר אותו רש לאותו עשיר</he> that poor (ignorant) man says to the rich man, teach me &c.

<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 9:2">Deut. R. s. 9</cite> <he>אתמול … ועכשיו הוא מסיח כרש וכ׳</he> yesterday he (Moses) spoke like a rich man (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 32:12">Ex. XXXII, 12</cite>; <cite ref="Numbers 14:19">Num. XIV, 19</cite>), but now he speaks like a poor man (begging, ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 3:23">Deut. III, 23</cite>); a. e.—Pl. <he>רָשִׁים</he>, <he>רָשִׁין</he>.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 31:7">Lev. R. s. 31</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Song of Songs 7:6">Cant. VII, 6</cite> <he>ודלת</he>) <he>הר׳ שבכם וכ׳</he> the poorest (in mind) among you are as precious to me as Elijah &c.; Cant. R. l. c.

<cite ref="Megillah 11a:16">Meg. 11ᵃ</cite> (play on <he>אחשורוֹשׁ</he>, <cite ref="Esther 1:1">Esth. I, 1</cite>) <he>שהכל נעשו רשין בימיו</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>רָאשִׁין</he>) all became poor in his days (with ref. to <cite ref="Esther 10:1">Esth. X, 1</cite>).
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 5:7:1">Koh. R. to V, 7</cite>, v. <cite ref="P01467"><he>עֵשָׂו</he></cite>; a. fr.
